text: Welcome to week five of the official
Arkhamards iRacing series. In this week,
you'll be taking on the Michigan
International Speedway for 25 laps. This
week in qualifying, you want to use your
warm-up laps to get familiar with your
ideal line. It may seem tempting to
chuck it down onto the flat through the
corners, but you'll find that there's
not nearly enough grip to maintain pace.
As a result, your best bet will be to
run a line higher and treat the first
seam as you would the white line at any
of the other intermediate tracks in the
schedule. Find this line as you continue
getting up to speed and building tire
temperature. Run the high line through
turns three and four at the end of your
first lap and throttle up out of the
corner to take the white flag. As you
head down into turns one and two, nearly
eclipsing 200 mph. Arc out as far as you
can. Give the throttle a slight lift and
get the car turned down the track,
aiming at that inside seat. Straddle it
with your left front. Get back on the
throttle as you apex around the red
Michigan USA logo on the wall and let
the car track up naturally on exit.
The outside wall will dump air on your
spoiler if you get too close. So once
you unwind the wheel and exit, give it
some room as you make your way down the
backstretch. Heading into turns three
and four, you want to hit the corner the
same as one and two. Arc out, fire the
car toward the inside with the lift and
straddle the seam through the center as
you get back on the throttle. Once you
reach the exit of turn four, allow the
car to continue rotating until you've
pointed at the apron, taking the
shortest route to the finish line to end
your run. Let's see that again.

Starting the race in second gear, you'll
find that the qualifying line will be
quicker and better for your tires in the
long run. But what will play an even
greater factor over the course of the
race will be the draft. To maintain
track position, I'd recommend finding a
place in line up against the wall in the
straightaways and using that position to
pick off your competition in the third
lane. As the race goes on, traffic in
that third lane can sometimes become
congested. So, if that becomes the case,
you can drop back down to the second
lane and use your tire advantage to
compensate for stepping outside of the
draft. But in order to do this, you'll
need to be patient early on in the race
and manage your tires well. You can do
this by staying in line and making use
of the entire racing surface, running
the second lane in the corners and
tracking out as high as traffic will
allow on the
straightaways. If you're fortunate
enough to qualify close to the front,
I'd recommend hooking up with the front
runners and making an attempt to pull
away from the field as everybody else
fights for position. If you can convince
the cars around you to run the optimal
lane and cooperate, you shouldn't have
any problems building a gap. But asking
for cooperation in an official race is a
tough ask. So you might just be better
off waiting in line and conserving your
tires. If you can keep your tires under
you, manage traffic, demonstrate your
understanding of the draft, you'll find
yourself fighting for the win as the
race winds down. Good luck.
